title: Lesson 75 - That's Not How It Was Explained to Me

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That’s not how it was explained to me. The group update says, “Maya won’t be joining because her schedule is too full.” That reads as a completed decision.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I understand why. Carla’s original note asked whether you would be open to a ten-minute talk and said there was no pressure. She also said she could contact you directly.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What exactly did you say in reply?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I wrote, “Her hospital training calendar is unusually full, so please don’t count on her. If you still need an answer, ask her directly next week.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Then I was told that I had declined, but your message actually combined a warning not to plan around me with permission to contact me later.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, although “please don’t count on her” may have been understood as the main answer. The direct-contact sentence came second and sounded optional.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: According to Carla’s group summary, my schedule was the reason for a final decision. The original source says only that she wanted to know whether I was open to being asked.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: The reply cites your full calendar, but it doesn’t report a decision you made. I haven’t found any sentence where you accepted or declined.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Can we trace “won’t be joining” back to an exact sentence?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: No. It appears to come from Carla’s interpretation of my warning, not from a direct reply by you.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I may have described Carla as changing your words, but that suggests intent we haven’t established. A more accurate version is that her summary made the status more final.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I agree. And I may have phrased my reply as if I had authority to set the expectation. That explains why the second sentence was easy to overlook.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: If we write, “Carla misunderstood,” we will repeat the same problem by claiming to know her mental process.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Then let’s write only what the record supports: I replied out of concern, but I wasn’t authorized to answer for you.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: We also need the current status. I haven’t accepted or declined, and I don’t want the group to wait while we discuss it.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: The role may already be filled. Could the correction say there is no need to reopen it, but future invitations should come directly to you?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. If the role is still open, Carla can send the details directly by Tuesday. I will answer her myself after checking my schedule.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I’ll send the correction to Carla privately first, not to the whole group. She can update the group only if the status still matters.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Read it back: “Ben replied before checking with Maya. Maya has not accepted or declined. Please contact her directly if an answer is still needed; otherwise no change is required.”

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: That keeps behavior, authority and status clear. It corrects the version without asking Carla to defend her intention or sharing our private conversation.
